Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>'

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. </UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>'

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>'

SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 33: The listed entity shall submit quarterly and year-to-date standalone financial results to the stock exchange within forty-five days of the end of each quarter (sixty days for annual audited financial results). Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. The historical compounding trajectory of the underlying asset class demonstrates a sustainable Return on Equity of 16.5% and a balanced Debt to Equity ratio of 0.45x. A rigorous 5,000-path Monte Carlo simulation projects the terminal wealth distribution for the anchor price of ₹17.99 over the 5-year horizon. Recent corporate news flow is characterized by regular, compliant disclosures filed with exchange authorities in accordance with statutory regulations. Macro sentiment is heavily influenced by central bank monetary policy shifts, real interest rate trajectories, and industrial metal consumption indices. Capital Deployment: Divide the ₹1,000,000.00 allocation into four equal tranches of ₹250,000.00. Execute tranche one immediately at the anchor price of ₹17.99. Deploy subsequent tranches systematically upon structural pullbacks or when volatility pushes pricing toward the P10 boundary.

Given the 1-year 95% Parametric Value at Risk of -21.4% and Conditional Value at Risk of -30.6%, portfolio-level stop-loss mandates are overridden by the long-term 5-year structural thesis, provided physical industrial demand metrics remain intact.
